title: Supreme and Universal Light
description: Supreme and Universal Light in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Moore wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 429 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Wisdom and Virtue sought from God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Su-preme and u-ni-ver-sal Light! Foun-tain of rea-son! Judge of right! Par-ent of good! whose bless-ings flow On all a-bove, and all be-low:

lines: Fountain of reason! Judge of right!
Parent of good! whose blessings flow
On all above, and all below:
Assist us, Lord, to act, to be,
What nature and thy laws decree;
Which from thy breathing spirit came!
The narrow view, the selfish aim;
But with a Christian zeal embrace
Whate'er is friendly to our race.
O Father, grace and virtue grant!
No more we wish, no more we want:
To know, to serve thee, and to love,
Is peace below, — is bliss above.

licence: Public domain: Henry Moore died in 1802.
credits: Words by Henry Moore (1732–1802), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
